title: Animal 'Facts' Everyone Still Believes (That Are Completely Wrong)

beats.say: Quick quiz. What does an ostrich do when it gets scared?
If you said it buries its head in the sand, congratulations. You've been lied to by a cartoon.
beats.text:
"IT BURIES
ITS HEAD IN
THE SAND"

beats.say: Today we're fixing the animal facts that your teacher, your uncle, and the entire internet got completely wrong.
Let's start with the ostrich. Ostriches do not bury their heads in the sand. Not when they're scared, not ever.
Think about it. An animal that suffocated itself every time it got nervous would not have survived very long.
What they actually do is dig a shallow hole in the ground as a nest, and lay their eggs in it.
Several times a day, they lower their heads into that hole to turn the eggs over.
From far away, it looks like the bird is head first in the dirt. It's not hiding. It's parenting.
And when an ostrich is in real danger, it does the reasonable thing. It runs at about seventy kilometers an hour, or it kicks hard enough to seriously hurt a lion.
beats.text:
70 KM/H
+ A KICK THAT
HURTS LIONS

beats.say: Next. The goldfish with a three second memory. People love this one, because it makes them feel better about forgetting why they walked into the kitchen.
It's completely wrong.
Researchers have trained goldfish to push levers for food, to react to sounds, and to show up at a certain spot at feeding time. And they remember these tricks for months.
So your goldfish isn't forgetting you every three seconds. It remembers you just fine. It just doesn't care.
beats.text:
IT REMEMBERS
YOU. IT JUST
DOESN'T CARE.

beats.say: Now, bulls and the color red.
The matador waves a red cape, the bull charges, so obviously the bull hates red. Except bulls can't really see red the way we do.
Cattle have two color vision, so to a bull, that bright red cape looks more like a dull, muddy brown.
What actually makes the bull charge is the movement. Wave a blue cape, a green cape, or your grandma's tablecloth, and you'll get the exact same result.
The red is for the crowd. It's not science. It's show business.
And blind as a bat? Bats are not blind. Not a single species.
Lots of bats use echolocation, but they can still see. And big fruit bats barely echolocate at all. They get around with sharp eyes and a great nose.
So really, the saying should be blind as a guy looking for the glasses that are on his head.
beats.text:
BLIND AS A GUY
LOOKING FOR
HIS GLASSES

beats.say: And we're just getting started, because the next one involves Disney, a cliff, and a very fake documentary.
